checks.rule: A legal boundary is an exact imaginary line and is rarely identified with precision on the ground or in conveyances.
A physical boundary feature may or may not coincide with the legal boundary.
Large-scale Ordnance Survey mapping is subject to survey tolerances.
The great majority of registered titles show general boundaries rather than exact legal boundaries.
There is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio relating a general boundary on an HMLR title plan to the legal boundary.
A determined-boundary process exists when an exact line is required.
Reject any workflow that equates general title-plan red edging with a surveyed legal boundary.
Require a boundary evidence class to be recorded before using boundary vertices for elevation sampling.
If only a general boundary is available, mark parcel-edge elevation as boundary-uncertain rather than exact.
Do not convert hedge, wall or fence depiction into legal-boundary certainty without corroborating evidence.
Do not assign a numeric legal-boundary tolerance where HMLR states no standard tolerance exists.
Preserve a fail-closed path for parcels whose exact boundary cannot be established from public evidence.
